# Blackmagic DeckLink SDK headers

Only the API `include/` directories are here, taken verbatim from the Blackmagic
DeckLink SDK 16.0. Nothing else from the SDK is vendored: the examples and,
importantly, the pre-compiled binaries (`DeckLinkAPI.framework`,
`libDeckLinkAPI.so`, the Windows typelibs) are not part of this tree.

- `Win/include` and `Mac/include` are the directories Blackmagic publishes in
  the SDK 16.0 download.
- `Linux/include` is the same SDK 16.0 header set as redistributed by the Fedora
  `decklink-devel` 16.0 package, which packages exactly these files.

`decklink-sys` finds these headers automatically when `--features hardware` is
enabled, so the hardware shim builds on Windows, macOS and Linux without a
separate SDK download. Set `DECKLINK_SDK_DIR` to use headers from a full SDK
install instead; the build prefers that directory when it is valid.

## Why the headers and not the whole SDK

The SDK as a whole is distributed under an end user licence that forbids
redistribution, and Blackmagic's developer support states that it is only to be
obtained from their site. The *headers*, however, carry a different licence: each
one opens with the Blackmagic Source License, which grants permission to "use,
reproduce, display, distribute, sub-license, execute, and transmit the Software"
provided the notice is kept. That is the same reasoning Chromium applies when it
checks these headers into `third_party/decklink`, recorded there as
`License: BSL (v 1.0)`, and the reasoning Fedora uses to ship them as
`decklink-devel`. So the headers travel with this repository and the binaries do
not.
